races.title: State House, District 113
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jake Johnson
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 113 since August 2019, when he was appointed to fill a vacancy. He was a Polk County commissioner from 2016 to 2019 and chaired the board from December 2017. He works as a real estate agent with Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices.
cands.gaps: We could not find his date of birth or when, if ever, he lived outside North Carolina. We found no documented statements from him on data centers, development or growth limits. His campaign site gives no specific positions on homestead property taxes, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, immigration or H-1B, or police pay. We found no bills he sponsored or actions in office tied to these issues. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2020 through 2026. We found no reliable endorsements and no documented controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia and his campaign site both say he was born and raised on a farm in Saluda in Polk County, and he still lives in Polk County.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Polk County commissioner from December 2016 to August 2019, including chairman from December 2017. Appointed to the NC House in August 2019 and re-elected in 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2026. Named House Deputy Majority Whip in 2023. Works in real estate.
qual.why: He has about seven years of legislative service plus earlier local elected office with a county board, and a private-sector real estate career. Committee posts were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: He has about seven years of legislative service plus earlier local elected office with a county board, and a private-sector real estate career. Committee posts were not counted toward the score.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he is pro-life and "will always fight for the unborn and the born," and that life should be protected.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he is a proud NRA member and believes the right to bear arms "should never be infringed upon."

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he favors the teacher pay raises already given and believes the state should do more to support educators. It does not mention vouchers or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia and his campaign site both say he was born and raised on a farm in Saluda in Polk County, and he still lives in Polk County.

cands.name: John Morgan
cands.bio: Retired U.S. Air Force Lieutenant Colonel (1972–1993) who flew reconnaissance missions and presidential airlift. Later a 747 captain and flight instructor with Atlas Air. Served as a Saluda city commissioner. Runs a small housing business with his wife. Democratic candidate for NC House District 113 in 2026.
cands.gaps: We could not find where John Morgan was born or raised. We also could not find the years he served as a Saluda city commissioner. We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, or policing. He has no legislative record, so no deeds could be documented. His campaign site lists funding public schools and supporting Medicaid as goals, but we found no specific bills or proposals.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign site says he and his wife moved to Saluda in 1997, about 29 years before the 2026 election; his birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Air Force manager and pilot for 21 years, retiring as Lt. Colonel. He says he managed multimillion-dollar military budgets and trained as an accountant, with a bachelor's in accounting and an MBA. He served as a Saluda city commissioner overseeing water and sewer, and co-owns a small housing business.
qual.why: Local elected office, budget management experience and business ownership put him in the middle range. He has no record of state legislative service.
qual.label: Local elected office, budget management experience and business ownership put him in the middle range. He has no record of state legislative service.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In his Ballotpedia candidate survey he said farmland preservation needs to be actively pursued and that the state's natural beauty needs to be shepherded.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: His campaign site says he and his wife moved to Saluda in 1997, about 29 years before the 2026 election; his birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia candidate survey he listed agriculture among his policy priorities and wrote: "Farmland preservation needs to be actively pursued."
